title: Profit target display follow-ups (batch PR #207) — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #207 (batched: frontend-trend-strength-chart-followups, frontend-volume-indicators-chart-followups, frontend-divergence-markers-followups, frontend-tide-region-chart-shading-followups, frontend-profit-target-display-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Both findings below isolate specifically to frontend-profit-target-display-followups' own changes (RewardRiskBadge.tsx and the new frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts) -- the PR's other four batched changes had no findings of any kind (see PR #207's review comment for the full verification detail across all five).

checklist.step: RewardRiskBadge.tsx's new `failureAriaLabel` prop (this PR) parameterizes the *content* of the warning icon's `aria-label`, but doesn't fix the pre-existing (not introduced by this PR) reason that label is never actually announced to a screen reader at all: MUI's `SvgIcon` (which `WarningAmberIcon` wraps) defaults `aria-hidden="true"` whenever no `titleAccess` prop is supplied, and neither the old nor the new code passes one -- confirmed live (PR #207 browser walkthrough, MU stock detail page): the rendered DOM has both `aria-hidden="true"` and `aria-label="Below the 2:1 minimum"` on the same `<svg>` simultaneously, and `aria-hidden="true"` removes an element from the accessibility tree regardless of any `aria-label` also present. Testing-library's `getByLabelText` (used by both the pre-existing and this PR's new RewardRiskBadge.test.tsx assertions) matches on the raw `aria-label` attribute directly, not a real accessibility-tree computation, so the existing unit tests pass despite this. Fix by either passing MUI's `titleAccess` prop (which also clears the default `aria-hidden`) instead of a bare `aria-label`, or explicitly overriding `aria-hidden={false}` alongside the existing `aria-label` prop.

The new frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts (PROFIT_TARGET_DEFINITION / PROFIT_TARGET_ELDER_CONTEXT_SUFFIX) is domain-specific content (Elder ch. 58's Tradebill 'A' target formula, Autoenvelope/channel height, protective stop, ch. 53's 2:1 rule) shared across exactly two features (features/stocks and features/portfolio), placed in `utils/` specifically to avoid a cross-feature registry import. This is a genuinely arguable case (not a clear-cut misplacement) given the task's own explicit, well-reasoned decisions entry, but it does read as in tension with Frontend.md §3's own placement test ('references a feature's domain concept... -> features/<domain>/'; `utils/` is documented as for helpers that are 'domain-agnostic', which this text isn't) -- `utils/insiderClusters.ts` is a prior, narrower precedent (a single-feature helper, not genuinely cross-feature content) that doesn't fully cover this case either. Worth either (a) documenting this specific pattern (domain-specific content genuinely shared by exactly two feature registries, where neither owns it and cross-importing one from the other is the established anti-pattern) as an explicit, named exception in Frontend.md §3 alongside the existing utils/ placement rule, or (b) reconsidering whether a small third location (e.g. a features/shared/ or similar) would fit this and any future same-shaped case better than `utils/`.

decisions.decision: Fixed RewardRiskBadge.tsx's warning icon to pass MUI's `titleAccess={failureAriaLabel}` alongside the existing `aria-label={failureAriaLabel}` (kept both, rather than replacing aria-label with titleAccess outright) -- titleAccess clears SvgIcon's default aria-hidden='true' and sets role='img', while the retained aria-label keeps the existing getByLabelText-based test/query pattern working unchanged. Added a regression assertion to RewardRiskBadge.test.tsx checking aria-hidden isn't 'true' and role is 'img'. For the second finding, went with option (a) from the finding itself: documented frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts's placement as a named, deliberate exception to Frontend.md §3's domain-agnostic utils/ rule, rather than inventing a new features/shared/ location. Implemented as part of a batched PR (#208) alongside four other unrelated small follow-up tasks, per explicit user instruction to batch remaining small followups onto one branch/PR.
decisions.rationale: Keeping aria-label alongside the new titleAccess (rather than dropping it) avoids a churny test-suite rewrite for every existing getByLabelText(...) call site referencing this component's aria-label convention, while still genuinely fixing the underlying accessibility bug the finding described -- aria-label wins over a <title> element in accessible-name computation anyway, so the two coexist without conflict. Chose (a) (document the exception) over (b) (a new features/shared/ location) because the finding itself frames (a) as the lower-risk, narrower fix ('a genuinely arguable case... worth documenting'), and a single instance of this shape (profitTargetHelpText.ts) doesn't yet justify standing up a whole new top-level directory with its own placement rules on spec -- the documented exception explicitly invites reusing this same pattern (not a new location) if a second same-shaped case appears, which keeps the option to introduce features/shared/ open later if a real pattern (not just one case) emerges.

comments.summary: Verified against MUI's actual SvgIcon source (frontend/node_modules/@mui/material/SvgIcon/SvgIcon.js): it sets `"aria-hidden": titleAccess ? undefined : true, role: titleAccess ? 'img' : undefined`. Before this fix, WarningAmberIcon had no titleAccess, so aria-hidden was unconditionally 'true' regardless of the aria-label prop -- a genuine bug, not a no-op concern. Passing titleAccess={failureAriaLabel} now clears aria-hidden and sets role='img'; the retained aria-label still wins accessible-name computation over the <title> element titleAccess also renders, so both coexist without conflict. This is a real, correctly-verified accessibility fix, not a subtly-wrong one.

The Frontend.md §3 named exception for utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts is placed appropriately (within the Structure rules subsection, immediately after the utils/ placement rule it amends) and reads as a genuinely arguable, well-reasoned carve-out rather than a precedent-setting workaround -- consistent with architecture-review's placement checklist.

review.notes: Part of a 5-task batched PR (#208). Full frontend suite (700 tests, 99.7%+ coverage), eslint, and tsc -b --noEmit all clean. No live interactive Playwright MCP browser walkthrough was performed for RewardRiskBadge specifically (no browser tool was available in this review session) -- substituted with the MUI source trace above, RewardRiskBadge.test.tsx's DOM-attribute assertions, and the full persisted e2e suite (18/18 passing, though no e2e spec currently exercises RewardRiskBadge directly -- stock-analysis.spec.ts doesn't assert on it).
